result.target_summary: Wealth classifiably managed loans are evaluated for non-accrual status based on internal risk classification rather than delinquency status; 72%, 85%, and 96% of these loans were rated investment grade as of December 31, 2024, 2023, and 2022, respectively.

target_year_over_year_context.explanation:
Both disclosures specify that End-of-Period (EOP) classifiably managed Private Bank loans are excluded from the delinquency numerator, denominator, and ratios. The 2024 disclosure (c_2024_7_D235) focuses on this exclusion rule, which matches the primary topic of c_2023_7_D205. Note that c_2023_7_D205 also mentions investment grade ratings, which are detailed in the linked c_2024_7_D236, but the core 'exclusion from delinquency metrics' topic aligns with D235.

This row captures the specific topic within c_2023_7_D205 regarding Wealth classifiably managed loans: they are evaluated for non-accrual/write-off based on internal risk classification (not solely delinquency) and details their investment grade ratings (85%, 96%, 94% in 2023/2022/2021). This corresponds exactly to the content in c_2024_7_D236, which covers the same evaluation methodology and provides the updated ratings (72%, 85%, 96% in 2024/2023/2022). While both relate to the same source disclosure, they represent distinct sub-topics (general exclusion vs. risk classification/ratings) that are fully captured by splitting into two rows, avoiding a spurious 1-to-1 merge with D235 which lacks the rating data.

comparisons.peer_topic: Consumer Loan Portfolio Composition and Credit Quality Statistics
comparisons.peer_summary: The company presents outstanding consumer loans, nonperforming loans, and past-due accruals in Table 19, with outstandings primarily consisting of auto and specialty lending ($54.9 billion), U.S. securities-based lending ($48.7 billion), and non-U.S. consumer loans ($2.8 billion) at December 31, 2024. Residential mortgage loans include fully-insured loans with curtailed interest, and the company excludes fully-insured and fair-value-option loans from certain credit quality statistics to better represent ongoing operations.
comparisons.comparison: Both C and BAC manage consumer loan portfolios with specific credit quality statistics and adjustments for certain loan types. C provides a specific breakdown of credit quality for 'Wealth classifiably managed loans,' noting that 72% were rated investment grade as of December 31, 2024, and excludes these from delinquency metrics. BAC presents outstanding consumer loans and credit quality statistics but excludes fully-insured loans and fair-value-option loans from certain credit quality statistics to better represent ongoing operations, focusing on auto, specialty lending, and securities-based lending.

sentences.text: As of December 31, 2024, 2023 and 2022, 72%, 85% and 96% of Wealth classifiably managed loans were rated investment grade.

We believe that the presentation of information adjusted to exclude the impact of the fully-insured loan portfolio and loans accounted for under the fair value option is more representative of the ongoing operations and credit quality of the business.

comparisons.peer_summary: The risk assessment process may include reviewing key metrics such as delinquency status, collateral value, FICO credit scores, and other risk factors where applicable.
comparisons.comparison: Both C and GS disclose that delinquency status is a key metric used in their credit risk assessment processes, although the specific application differs. C explicitly states that for its Wealth classifiably managed loans, delinquency metrics are excluded from specific tables because non-accrual status is determined by internal risk classification rather than delinquency status alone. GS broadly discloses that its risk assessment process includes reviewing delinquency status, collateral value, and FICO scores, indicating delinquency remains a relevant factor in their general credit evaluation framework.

comparisons.peer_topic: Wholesale credit exposure maturity and ratings profile disclosure
comparisons.peer_summary: Tables present the maturity and internal risk ratings profiles of the wholesale credit portfolio as of December 31, 2024 and 2023, with investment grade defined as BBB-/Baa3 or higher.
comparisons.comparison: Both C and JPM define 'investment grade' using internal risk ratings. C states that a significant majority (72%) of its Wealth classifiably managed loans were rated investment grade, relying on internal risk classification. JPM similarly defines investment grade for its wholesale credit portfolio as internal ratings with qualitative characteristics equivalent to BBB-/Baa3 or higher, noting that collateral and structural support are considered in determining these internal risk ratings.

sentences.text: As of December 31, 2024, 2023 and 2022, 72%, 85% and 96% of Wealth classifiably managed loans were rated investment grade.

The Firm generally considers internal ratings with qualitative characteristics equivalent to BBB-/Baa3 or higher as investment grade, and takes into consideration collateral and structural support when determining the internal risk rating for each credit facility.

comparisons.peer_summary: Consumer borrower evaluation is tailored to lending type, with securities-based loans assessed by collateral quality and volatility, and residential real estate loans evaluated using debt-to-income ratios, net worth, and credit scores like FICO.
comparisons.comparison: Both C and MS evaluate consumer credit quality using factors beyond simple delinquency, incorporating collateral and internal assessments. C excludes delinquency metrics for its Wealth classifiably managed loans, relying on internal risk classification and credit ratings (investment grade status). MS evaluates securities-based loans based on collateral quality, volatility, and liquidity, and residential real estate loans using credit-scoring models (e.g., FICO scores) and debt-to-income ratios, indicating a similar reliance on fundamental credit factors and collateral rather than just payment history.
